$comment: The map of the wiki. Every feature has a usage page, a developer chapter and its screenshots; scripts/build-wiki.ts fails CI when a page, a screenshot or a link is missing, so a feature cannot land without its docs. Order here is the order in the sidebar.

usage.summary: Install Git Manager, open your first folder and find your way around the window.
Open folders with many repositories, add more folders, and save a workspace to a file.
Browse your files and see at a glance what git thinks of each one.
Create, rename, copy, move and trash files and folders right in the Files panel.
Edit files in tabs, jump between changes and keep an eye on what you changed.
Multiple cursors, the Code menu, Go to Line and the IDE features of the editor.
Line spacing, visible whitespace, the cursor, word wrap, indentation detected from each file, and zoom.
Edit Markdown with a toolbar, a live preview, diagrams, and a rich editor for the finished page.
Open images and PDFs in a preview tab that frees its memory when closed, and compare two versions in a diff.
Find files, classes, symbols and text in the whole workspace with double Shift.
The editor's find and replace bar, and Replace in Files across the workspace.
Stage what you want, write a message and commit, per repository.
The buttons and the ... menu of each repository in Changes: branch, Sync, Commit and more.
Commit and push in one go, and sign-off, author, GPG signing and skipping hooks.
Add files, folders or extensions to .gitignore from a right-click.
Compare a file with its last commit side by side and stage single hunks.
What to do when a merge, rebase or cherry-pick stops on conflicts.
The three pane merge tool: take changes from either side and check the result.
See who changed a line, when and why, and jump to that commit.
Browse the commit graph, read commits and undo or copy them.
Create, switch, merge, rebase, rename and delete branches, and browse tags.
The JetBrains-style branch list: checkout, compare, update, push and merge any branch.
Fetch, pull and push, and what the ahead and behind numbers mean.
Put work aside and bring it back later.
Put chosen changes aside as a named patch and bring them back, in full or file by file.
Every git command in one JetBrains-style menu, including the current file's history.
Push, Pull, Update Project, Merge, Rebase, Reset, Rollback, Remotes and Clone, with their options.
Reorder, reword, squash, edit and drop commits before you share them.
Check out several branches of one repository in separate folders.
Repositories inside a repository: see their changes and init, update, add or remove them.
Large files stored with Git LFS: badges, sizes in diffs, track patterns, pull and prune.
Sign in to GitHub to share a project, sync a fork and create gists.
Every git command the app ran, with its output (off by default).
Run shells below the editor or in a tab, with several terminals and your own shell and font.
Split terminals, find in the output, Cmd+click file paths, drop files, rename, and the optional parts.
Run npm, Composer, Make, Deno and just scripts with one click, with the right Node version.
Back and Forward across files, diffs and commits.
The menu bar: what is in each menu, and how its keys work.
Every setting, where it is saved, and the light and dark themes.
Pick a light and a dark color theme from 37, including high contrast ones.
Every option of the Terminal, GitHub and Automation sections of Settings.
What is in ~/.gitmanager, editing settings.json by hand, and fixing a broken file.
How Git Manager tells you about new versions, and the beta channel.
The status bar, picking the active repository, and how to report a bug or ask for a feature.
The memory readout, its breakdown and GPU rows, and the debug memory log.
Let AI tools such as Claude Code, and scripts in a terminal, use Git Manager safely.
Use Git Manager as the merge tool for git on the command line.
Every keyboard shortcut on one page.
The keys of the editor, the find bar, Markdown, the merge tool, lists and dialogs.
Common problems and how to fix them.
Git not found, failing hooks, signing in and common git errors.

developer.summary: Start here: set up the project, run it, and find your way around these pages.
How the Rust backend, the Svelte frontend and git fit together.
What lives in which folder and file.
Tauri commands, the git read and write split, errors, the CLI runner and the file watcher.
The file watcher: how each file event becomes a repository or folder refresh.
Workspace files, VS Code compatibility and which folders reopen at start.
The gmpreview URL scheme: how previews stream images and PDFs to the web view, safely and in pieces.
The terminal, search, scripts, Git Console, GitHub, MCP and other Rust services, and how they stay idle until used.
Split groups, find, file links, drops and the terminal addons, each lazy and switchable.
The shell, stores, Svelte 5 runes, the API bridge, keys, menus and colors.
How Preview Only edits the page and writes changes back block by block without reformatting the file.
How Open Repository in Browser and the GitHub link items turn remote URLs into web pages.
How one key press runs either a page handler or a menu item, never both.
The feature folders in src/lib, their stores, and what loads only on first use.
The blame bugs we found, why they happened and how we fixed them.
The update check and link bugs we found, why they happened and how we fixed them.
The status bar and Help link bugs we found, why they happened and how we fixed them.
The Changes tab opened from the status bar: every uncommitted file compared with the last commit.
State fields, compartments, widgets, keymaps and update rules for every text pane.
The editor cursor settings: shapes, blinking, smooth movement and extra caret height.
Auto-close, completion, folding, indent guides, the margin line and the languages, each switchable and lazy.
The slim bar above the code: breadcrumbs, badges and icon actions, and how it collapses when narrow.
Index of the backend commands, plus every event and channel.
Every settings.json and state.json key with its default, range and where it is used.
Commands for folders, status, staging, commits, diffs, conflicts, stashes, the shelf and ignore files.
Commands for branches, merge and rebase dialogs, interactive rebase, fetch, pull, push, remotes, clone, patches and tags.
Commands for the log, blame, file history, reset, worktrees, submodules, Git LFS and GitHub.
Commands for files, config, the memory log, search, scripts, the terminal, the Git Console and the MCP server.
How the Rust and Vitest suites work, test repositories and what to test.
Every Vitest and Rust test file, folder by folder, and what it covers.
Web view devtools, Rust logs, reading IPC errors and common dead ends.
Inspect, measure and drive the running app with the MCP tools and git-manager cli.
CI, the beta and stable release workflows, and the wiki deploy.
Where the version lives, the changelog rules and scripts/version.ts.
Code signing and notarization, and the plan for Windows and Linux.
How this wiki is built, how screenshots are taken, and keeping docs in sync.
Code style, commits, pull requests and the docs checklist.
